title: ArtSide
summary: A camera-enabled museum companion adjusts its spoken guidance to the artwork and the visitor.

offers.interpretation: ArtSide grounds a conversation in the artwork a visitor is looking at and lets the visitor set the pace.
offers.dialogue: ArtSide proposes shifting between explaining an artwork and asking the visitor a question.

applications.interpretation: In ArtSide, try offering two readings of the same artwork and letting the visitor choose which detail to explore.
applications.dialogue: In ArtSide, first acknowledge what the visitor noticed, then ask which detail in the artwork supports that reading.

title: Associative Multi-Agent Network Design for Creativity
summary: An associative network distributes features across agents, shares cues between them and leaves idea selection to the person.

offers.interpretation: Brooke and David propose giving different features to different agents so the person can choose among the ideas they generate.

applications.interpretation: Try letting the person select one feature of the original prompt before your agents generate their next round of ideas.
applications.dialogue: Test whether assigning one agent to extend an idea and another to question it produces different ideas from open discussion.

title: Wise(r) Mind
summary: A biosignal-informed reflection system separates acknowledging a person's feelings from questioning their choices.

offers.dialogue: Wise(r) Mind gives two agents different jobs: one acknowledges a feeling, and the other questions a choice.

applications.interpretation: After the two agents reflect on an episode, let the person choose which perspective to revisit instead of merging both into one conclusion.
applications.dialogue: Try letting the person decide when the conversation moves from describing an episode to asking what they might do differently.
